title: Clause Evaluation Run
statement: Let $C$ be a clause over variables indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, and let $r$ and $u$ be binary words such that every variable index occurring in $C$ is less than $|u|$. For any binary words $x$ and $p$ satisfying $x=p\mathbin{++}\mathrm{pair}(\mathrm{enc}(C)\mathbin{++}r,u)$, and any Boolean accumulator $c$, there is a time $t\le 3|\mathrm{enc}(C)|$ such that the verifier, started in the clause-evaluation state with accumulator $c$, having consumed $|p|$ input bits, with work word $u$ and work head at $0$, reaches a configuration having consumed $|p|+2|\mathrm{enc}(C)|$ input bits, work word $u$, and work head at $0$. Its state is the verdict state carrying false if $c$ is true and every literal in $C$ is satisfied by the assignment read from $u$; otherwise its state is the formula-level evaluation state.
hypotheses_covered: $C$ is a clause over natural-number variables
Every variable index in $C$ is less than $|u|$
replaced:
Let $C$ be a list of literals whose variable indices are all below $|u|$ for a word
$u$, let $\sigma$ be its serialization, and let the input be
$x = p \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathrm{pair}(\sigma \mathbin{+\!\!+} r, u)$. Started in the
clause-level evaluation state with accumulator $c$, $|p|$ bits consumed, work word $u$,
and head $0$, the non-tautology verifier within some $t \le 3|\sigma|$ steps has
consumed $|p| + 2|\sigma|$ bits, has head $0$, and is in the verdict state with bit $0$
if $c$ holds and every literal of $C$ is satisfied by the assignment read off $u$, and
in the formula-level evaluation state otherwise.
